decisions.reason: It fits the firm's core proposition of trusted second-channel communication, complements existing identity products, and is likely inexpensive to keep as a software-based option while demand continues to develop.

This architecture-level security offering is highly aligned with the firm's cryptography capabilities and long-term move toward integrated secure digital ecosystems, so management would likely retain it as a strategic platform option.

Although it matches high-compliance use cases, a hardware signature token is costlier and more niche to maintain than software options, and the firm's direction appears to favor broader app-based and cross-channel security solutions.

The compliance suite is somewhat narrower than the firm's main identity stack, but it still leverages regulatory-security know-how and can be kept at relatively low cost until its market potential becomes clearer.
